questions.q: Why can't a Governor contract safely use a plain ERC-20's live balanceOf for voting weight?
options: A holder could acquire tokens right before a vote and sell them right after, with no real stake in the outcome
Live balances always return zero for security reasons
balanceOf is not a real Solidity function
ERC-20 tokens cannot have more than one holder
questions.explain: The lesson explains that checkpointed voting power exists specifically to prevent a holder from gaming a live balance around a vote.

questions.q: In the GovernanceToken contract, which single internal function do current OpenZeppelin versions route every transfer, mint, and burn through, and which this contract must override?
options: _mintOrBurn
_update
_transfer
_checkpoint
questions.explain: The code and narration both identify _update as the one hook ERC20Votes needs overridden, replacing the older separate _transfer/_mint/_burn hooks.

questions.q: Why must GovernanceToken override the nonces function at all, given that ERC20Permit and Nonces agree on its implementation?
options: Because nonces is deprecated and must be deleted
Because both parent contracts declare nonces, and Solidity requires an explicit override to resolve the collision
Because ERC20Permit does not support nonces at all
Because overriding nonces disables delegation
questions.explain: The lesson states this override exists purely to satisfy Solidity's rule about resolving a function declared by two parent contracts, even when they agree.

questions.q: A holder mints and receives governance tokens but never calls delegate(). What is their voting power on a proposal?
options: Equal to their full token balance automatically
Double their token balance
Negative, as a penalty for not delegating
Zero, because ERC20Votes tracks voting power per delegate, not automatically per holder
questions.explain: The lesson calls out forgetting to delegate as the most common reason a new governance token appears to report zero voting power in testing.

questions.q: What practical benefit does ERC20Permit add to this governance token beyond standard ERC-20 approvals?
options: It removes the need for a constructor
It automatically doubles a holder's voting power
It lets a holder delegate or approve using a signature instead of a separate on-chain transaction
It prevents the token from ever being transferred
questions.explain: The lesson notes ERC20Permit enables gas-free, signature-based delegation or approval, which matters for a frontend-driven delegation flow.
